clue.text: Morning's end sees return of bad atmosphere

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters built so far are read from right to left

parts.note: AM is the abbreviation for morning, plus the possessive S
an end is a goal or purpose

explanation.surface: A grim morning drawing to a close in a foul, oppressive mood.
explanation.walkthrough: AM'S + AIM, read backwards, spells MIASMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A miasma is an unpleasant, unhealthy vapour or a pervading oppressive feeling hanging in the air.

clue.text: Staff warning — women not welcome here?

definitions.note: the question mark flags a descriptive definition of a place

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
cave (Latin 'beware') is old British schoolboy slang shouted as a warning

explanation.surface: A notice warning employees that women are unwelcome somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: CAVE, pronounced 'kay-vee', was shouted by British schoolchildren as a lookout's warning that a teacher was coming.
explanation.definitionFit: A man cave is a den or shed reserved for a man's hobbies and relaxation, notionally off-limits to his partner.

clue.text: Insect sheltered under a pinhead

indicators.note: in a down answer, under puts the word for sheltered beneath what comes before it, so it is written last

parts.note: taken as written
the head of a pin is its opening letter
to shelter someone is to hide them

explanation.surface: A tiny insect taking cover beneath the head of a pin.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'under' places the word for sheltered beneath A and the pin's head: A + P + HID.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking bug such as a greenfly or blackfly.

clue.text: Spoil little kid that really divides opinion

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
a mite is an affectionate word for a small child

explanation.surface: Ruining a small child is something people argue fiercely about.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a British yeast-extract spread famously marketed with the slogan 'love it or hate it'.
explanation.definitionFit: The spread is so notoriously polarising that its name is used for anything people either adore or loathe.

clue.text: Energy content of vegetation on which we live

indicators.note: content sits inside its holder, so the first item goes within the second

parts.note: plant life is vegetation
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: The energy stored in plants is what keeps us alive.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth is the world humans inhabit, a body orbiting the sun.

clue.text: Mean gossip

definitions.meaning: second meaning: inside information or the true facts

explanation.walkthrough: As an adjective it is usually hyphenated (a low-down trick); as a noun it is one word (give me the lowdown).
explanation.definitionFit: A low-down act is contemptible, and getting the lowdown means receiving the inside story or rumours.

clue.text: Dreamt one rebuilt a French cathedral

indicators.note: something rebuilt is put together again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dreamt that a French cathedral was rebuilt, as Notre-Dame is being after its fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Notre-Dame de Paris is the famous Gothic cathedral on the Île de la Cité.

clue.text: Dry riser in energy generator

indicators.note: in a down answer a riser climbs upwards, so the word for dry is written bottom to top

parts.note: brut describes very dry champagne
taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A dry riser is a fire-fighting pipe in a building, here oddly found in a power generator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry riser' reads as one plumbing term; it splits into a wine word and its upward-reading instruction. 'Energy generator' looks like the definition but energy is needed for E.
explanation.definitionFit: A turbine is a machine whose rotor is driven by a fluid flow to produce power, as in a wind or steam generator.

clue.text: Base where society is hiding tyrant

indicators.note: 'where society is hiding' places one item tucked away inside the base word

parts.note: a depot is a base for vehicles or supplies
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A dictator lurking in a secret base, concealed from society.
explanation.definitionFit: A despot is an absolute ruler who wields power cruelly or oppressively.

clue.text: A crew that's under-represented creates new situation

indicators.note: to re-present something is to set it out again differently, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An understaffed ship's crew finds itself facing something unfamiliar.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen in 'under-represented' disguises the split: 'under' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in uncharted waters is an idiom for facing an unfamiliar, unprecedented set of circumstances.

clue.text: Hindu pacifist engaged in booing and hissing

indicators.note: something engaged in a phrase is held within it, so the letters run across the following words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A peaceful Hindu leader caught up in a jeering crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Mahatma Gandhi led India's independence movement through non-violent resistance, rooted in his Hindu faith.

clue.text: Pitch one made strange as it sounds

indicators.note: making something strange alters it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A singer's note made to sound odd, apparently on purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A phonetic spelling represents speech directly, writing each word according to its pronunciation.

clue.text: Suffocated by temperature: it couldn't be closer

parts.note: one who has suffocated has died
heat is a measure of temperature

explanation.surface: Someone overcome by stifling heat in a race too tight to call.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race or contest where competitors finish level, the narrowest possible result.

clue.text: Servant climbing damaged trees to get ring widths

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means going upwards, so the word for servant reads from the bottom

parts.note: a maid is a female servant

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters of trees are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A servant clambering up storm-damaged trees to measure their growth rings.
explanation.definitionFit: A diameter is the distance across a circle through its centre, so it measures how wide each ring is.

clue.text: Narrative account editor gutted is now in better order

indicators.note: gutting removes the insides, leaving only the first and last letter of each word

parts.note: outer letters of the first word
outer letters of the second word
outer letters of the third word

explanation.surface: A story cut down by its editor now reads more tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gutted' applies to all three words before it, not just editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Neater means tidier or more orderly, the comparative of neat.

clue.text: Blank sign that you can enter bog

definitions.text: sign that you can enter bog
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word shown on a lavatory door lock when nobody is inside

explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a toilet, not a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means empty or unoccupied, which is why it appears on a free toilet cubicle's indicator.

clue.text: Planes race to carry back store of arms

indicators.note: going back means reading from right to left
the two words carry the letters within them, so they run across the word break

parts.note: runs from inside the first word into the second

explanation.surface: Aircraft racing to bring munitions home.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a stockpile of weapons or the building where they are kept.

clue.text: Wire three times? Strange way to send short message

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal order, so the collected letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time, written three times

explanation.surface: Sending a telegram three times over seems an odd way to deliver a brief note.
explanation.walkthrough: To wire once meant to send a telegram, a fitting decoy for a messaging service.
explanation.definitionFit: Twitter, now renamed X, was the social platform built around posts originally limited to 140 characters.

clue.text: Showing a surplus, having incorporated Republican amendment

parts.note: Inc. is the abbreviation for incorporated, as in company names
R is the abbreviation for Republican
an edit is an amendment to a text

explanation.surface: A financial statement showing profit after a Republican change was written in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incorporated' reads as a containment signal but simply gives its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account is in credit when it holds a positive balance rather than an overdraft.

clue.text: Print technique used to protect squids

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a printer that sprays fine droplets onto paper
second meaning: the dark squirt a squid releases to escape predators

explanation.definitionFit: Inkjet printers fire tiny droplets, and a squid literally ejects a jet of ink as a smokescreen.

clue.text: It can make wine from cat water in France

parts.note: chat is French for cat
eau is French for water

explanation.surface: A recipe claiming French cat-water can be turned into wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' covers both words: each is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: In Bordeaux a château is a wine estate, and its name labels the wine it produces.

clue.text: Rather stained potty

indicators.note: potty means crazy, so the letters go haywire and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A child's potty that is rather the worse for stains.
explanation.walkthrough: Potty is British slang for mad as well as a child's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words introduce a preferred alternative: 'I'd rather walk' and 'I'll walk instead' do the same job.

clue.text: Having lost weight, squander chance to be a star

indicators.note: having lost something means it has gone, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for weight
to squander is to waste
a risk is a chance of something bad

explanation.surface: A dieter who throws away the chance to become famous.
explanation.walkthrough: WASTE without its W, then RISK.
explanation.definitionFit: An asterisk is the small star-shaped symbol used in printing.

clue.text: The way to go when solving this type of clue

definitions.text: The way to go when solving this type of clue

parts.note: surface reading: the best approach or method
setter's reading: the direction this very clue is written in the grid

explanation.walkthrough: The clue is self-referential: its own entry runs horizontally, so the direction to go is the label of its clue list.
explanation.definitionFit: Horizontal entries in a crossword are filled from left to right, the direction named by this word.

clue.text: Lists item dropped by riot teams

indicators.note: something dropped is let go, so those letters are taken out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: the letters to remove, one at a time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detail left out of the paperwork by police riot squads.
explanation.walkthrough: Strike out I, T, E and M from RIOTTEAMS, leaving R, O, T, A, S.
explanation.definitionFit: A rota is a schedule listing who does which duty and when.

clue.text: Terribly rude, when theatre is off

indicators.note: something done terribly goes badly wrong, so the following letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Complaining that it is awfully rude when a theatre show is cancelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like it describes the cancelled show, but it is the definition in its sense of unwell.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling off and being under the weather are both idioms for being slightly ill.

clue.text: Temptation to acquire stone showing such radiance

indicators.note: acquiring something takes it in, so one item is placed inside the other

parts.note: a lure is a temptation
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight

explanation.surface: The allure of a gem lies in its brilliant sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the gentle shine or glow reflected from a surface, a kind of brilliance.

clue.text: Swore when son landed in pickled

indicators.note: landing in a place means ending up inside it, so one letter goes within the other word

parts.note: food cured in brine or vinegar is preserved, like pickles
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent swearing when their boy came home drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Pickled is also slang for drunk, which the surface leans on.
explanation.definitionFit: To curse is to use bad language, so someone who cursed swore.
